hens_rule_text: As of a July 2025 ordinance (7-2 council vote) that lifted a roughly 20-year ban, up to 8 laying hens are allowed on single-family residential lots under 2 acres, kept in a fenced enclosure in the rear yard.
permit_notes: News coverage of the 2025 ordinance describes housing and care standards rather than a permit system; no separate city permit for keeping hens was found. Before this ordinance, chickens required agricultural zoning or a lot over 5 acres.
setback_notes: Hens must be kept in a fenced enclosure in the rear yard; no specific neighbor-setback distance in feet was found in available coverage. On agriculturally zoned land, barns/buildings housing livestock or fowl must be 150 ft from any property line, but this figure applies to ag-zoned lots, not the new residential hen rule.
coop_rules: Predator-proof hen house required; rules cover food storage and waste removal. Older agricultural-zone standard (may still apply there) called for enclosures at least 18 inches high with 10 sq ft of floor area per fowl.
zoning_notes: New rule applies to single-family residential lots and other residential zones under 2 acres; roosters, other fowl, hatching chicks and selling chicken products remain banned in residential zones and are only allowed on agriculturally zoned land.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

The exact codified section number and residential setback distance were not found; per batch instructions, no Tennessee state law overrides local rules and a 2024 state bill to protect small flocks did not pass.
